newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks close higher mirroring Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks close higher mirroring Wall Street.

text.p: Madrid stocks ended sharply higher on Tuesday, catching up with recent gains on Wall Street and underpinned by ongoing prospects for a rate cut here, dealers said.
The general index rose 4.19 points, 1.03 percent, to 411.26 and Ibex added 49.07 points, 1.04 percent, to 4,753.18.

Expectations of a cut in the Bank of Spain's key money rate from 6.75 percent on Friday, along with benign November inflation data due on the same day continued at the main focus of the market amid a lack of corporate news, dealers said.
Telefonica was particularly strong in run-up to a public share offering in early 1997. It rose 40 pesetas to 2,940.
"The market has gone back into the highs zone and the most logical thing is for prices to stabilise, although good medium term forecasts could keep pressuring upwards," said a trader.
Stocks may well move ahead again on Wednesday, but dealers were not ruling out early losses, depending on New York's close.
